description: Hello. We are a team of 6 CSE students from Dhaka, Bangladesh.
summary: Mohashunnyo is a 3D educational mission-design and Mars exploration game. Players learn how certain decisions taken throughout a space mission can affect not just the outcome but every stage of the mission from take-off to landing back home. They must work within a limited budget to design a spacecraft, manage mass, power, life support and risk, survive the journey to Mars, establish a habitat, explore data-based Martian terrain, collect scientific evidence and return safely to Earth. The game converts real NASA observations into gameplay decisions, in hopes of helping players develop scientific curiosity and problem-solving skills.
details:
Mohashunnyo is a 3D space mission design and Mars exploration game made with Godot 4. Players explore a generated Martian landscape, operate a rover, gather resources (evidences), deploy equipment purchased during mission design, and make decisions based on real observational data.

We aim to make mission planning and space exploration engaging and memorable through a visual, interactive game that combines archived NASA Mars elevation data and Perseverance MEDA weather observations with in-game labeled simulations. Players can explore different terrain regions (generated through various seeds), analyze what they come across during their exploration, and build a functioning outpost until the mission succeeds or fails. The game also distinguishes real data from fictional scenarios so players can learn the origins of the data and its limits.

The game was developed in Godot using GDScript and 3D assets. It uses NASA’s MOLA elevation data, MEDA weather products, NASA’s Space Exploration Vehicle and Z-2 spacesuit models, CC0 materials from ambientCG, and CC0 MakeHuman characters from MMWilliams/char-kit. The terrain, facilities, equipment, gameplay systems, and audio compositions were generated for the game based on our initial ideas and rough iterations. We had to consider the scientific accuracy of the simulations based on the datasets while balancing it with educational game abstractions.

Games can be an effective method to learn real information in a more engaging way, inspiring people to learn about space missions and the forefront of space research, especially with NASA's visions of Mars Missions, in a more fun way, reeling in potential future space enthusiasts and aspiring professionals while nurturing their scientific curiosity, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
